bookJourney.focus:
Preface - Scope, Status, and Method
This book is a survey, an architectural synthesis, and a programme of research. It does not present SOP Lang dynamic circuits as a completed theory of language or as a production-ready replacement for large language models. It asks whether a persistent symbolic system can acquire reusable linguistic and reasoning competence, construct a small executable circuit for each request, and expose enough of that construction to support inspection, replay, bounded exec

bookJourney.chapters: Abstract
bookJourney.focus:
Abstract
Scientific communication remains centred on prose documents even when the underlying work depends on data, software, formal models, statistical tests, simulation pipelines, and complex chains of evidence. Large language models have made those documents easier to search, summarize, critique, and transform, and the rapid development of scientific agents in 2025 and 2026 shows that models can already propose hypotheses, use tools, run experiments, analyse results, and draft manuscripts. A.1 Declarations, commands, values, and references
The research programme deliberately keeps the globally reserved syntax of SOP Lang small. A declaration begins with an output variable and a command expression. The remainder of the declaration is an ordered argument block that may continue over as many physical lines as needed. The block ends when the parser encounters the next declaration beginning with @. This makes line breaks primarily a readability mechanism rather than a semantic boundary

A SOP Lang circuit is the dependency structure induced by a set of declarations. No separate edge syntax is required. If one declaration contains $x, it depends on the value associated with x. If it contains ~x, it depends on the existence and identity of x at the meta-level, although whether it also forces evaluation of x depends on the command and runtime contract.

They are contracts attached to commands, subcircuits, registries, and receipts. An implementation may encode them as metadata, privileged commands, or host-level policy. What matters is that a runtime can distinguish proposal from evidence and evidence from authority.

A directed graph contains nodes connected by directed edges. A directed acyclic graph, or DAG, contains no directed cycle. If an edge means that one computation needs a value produced by another, the graph becomes a dataflow graph. A topological ordering of a DAG schedules every producer before its consumers. SOP Lang’s $var references induce exactly this kind of dependency for the acyclic portion of a circuit.
